py-pep758-313-list.title: Multiple exception types require parentheses on supported Python versions
py-pep758-313-list.description: The project supports Python 3.13 and excludes 3.14. In Python 3.13, multiple exception types in an `except` clause must be parenthesized, so this changed clause prevents the module from parsing and the handler cannot run.
py-pep758-313-list.evidence: The effective `requires-python` range is `>=3.13,<3.14`; the changed clause is `except ValueError, TypeError:`. Python 3.13 does not accept this syntax.
py-pep758-313-list.suggestion: Parenthesize the exception types for compatibility with the supported Python range.

py-pep758-313-group.title: Handler uses syntax unsupported by the configured Python range
py-pep758-313-group.description: The project supports Python 3.13 but excludes 3.14. In Python 3.13, an `except*` clause with multiple exception types must use a parenthesized tuple, so this changed clause causes the module to fail parsing on a supported interpreter.
py-pep758-313-group.evidence: The configured `requires-python` is `>=3.13,<3.14`; line 4 uses `except* ValueError, TypeError:`.
py-pep758-313-group.suggestion: Parenthesize the exception types so the clause parses on Python 3.13.

py-pep758-314-list-as.title: Parenthesize multiple exception types when using as
py-pep758-314-list-as.description: This `except` clause lists multiple exception types with `as` but does not enclose them in parentheses. Python 3.14 requires parentheses for this form, so the module fails to parse.
py-pep758-314-list-as.evidence: The changed clause is `except ValueError, TypeError as error:`. The configured supported Python range is `>=3.14,<3.15`, where multiple exception types with `as` require parentheses.
py-pep758-314-list-as.suggestion: Write the exception types as a parenthesized tuple.

py-pep758-314-group-as.title: Invalid syntax for grouped except* types
py-pep758-314-group-as.description: This handler uses an unparenthesized comma-separated type list with `except*` and `as`. Python 3.14 still requires multiple exception types in an `except*` clause to be parenthesized, so the module cannot be parsed under the repository's declared Python 3.14 requirement.
py-pep758-314-group-as.evidence: The changed clause is `except* ValueError, TypeError as error:`. The project requires Python `>=3.14,<3.15`; the supported grammar requires parentheses around multiple types when binding with `as`.
py-pep758-314-group-as.suggestion: Parenthesize the exception types, for example `except* (ValueError, TypeError) as error:`.

py-pep758-mixed-range.title: Multiple exception types need parentheses on Python 3.13
py-pep758-mixed-range.description: The project supports Python 3.13, but this clause uses the Python 3.14 PEP 758 syntax for multiple exception types without parentheses. Python 3.13 cannot parse the module, preventing it from loading on a supported runtime.
py-pep758-mixed-range.evidence: The changed clause is `except ValueError, TypeError:`. The supported range includes Python 3.13; the provided parser observation only confirms parsing under Python 3.14.6.
py-pep758-mixed-range.suggestion: Parenthesize the exception types to retain compatibility with Python 3.13.

py-pep758-unbound-handler.title: Undefined exception name masks the ValueError
py-pep758-unbound-handler.description: When `ValueError("sentinel")` is raised, Python evaluates the exception types in the handler. `MissingError` is undefined in this module, so evaluating the clause raises `NameError` instead of catching the `ValueError`. The clause is valid syntax under the specified Python 3.14 configuration; the defect is the runtime name lookup.
py-pep758-unbound-handler.evidence: The changed clause names `MissingError`, which the scenario states is neither defined nor imported anywhere in the complete module; the preceding `raise ValueError("sentinel")` reaches that handler.
py-pep758-unbound-handler.suggestion: Remove `MissingError` or replace it with an exception type defined or imported by the module.
